questions.q: Who is named as the Technical Service Owner for Patient Scheduling Application Service?
options: The Director of Patient Access
The Infrastructure Team Lead for Clinical Systems
The database administration team
Nobody — Technical Services don't require an owner
questions.explain: The Infrastructure Team Lead for Clinical Systems owns the Technical Service and is accountable for its mapping to the Business Service staying correct. The Director of Patient Access owns the Business Service above it.

questions.q: Why does this governance plan use three different review frequencies instead of one?
options: Because a single frequency is required by ServiceNow and can't be changed
Because different problems surface at different speeds — dashboard regressions, mapping drift, and whether a CI is still needed each need their own cadence
Three frequencies are used purely to create more paperwork
Monthly, quarterly, and annual reviews all check exactly the same thing
questions.explain: Monthly catches dashboard regressions, quarterly catches mapping drift, and annual re-certification catches CIs that are no longer needed or correctly classified — each at the pace that problem actually appears.

questions.q: What does an 'orphaned CI' on the Health Dashboard almost always indicate?
options: That the CI has too many relationships documented
That someone added infrastructure without documenting how it connects to anything else
That the CI has been successfully decommissioned
That Discovery is scanning the CI too frequently
questions.explain: A CI showing no relationships at all is a strong signal that it was added outside the governance process this lesson sets up.

questions.q: What is checked during the annual re-certification review?
options: Only whether the CI's name is spelled correctly
Whether each CI is still needed, still correctly classified, and still has accurate relationships
Only the Business Service Owner's job title
Whether the MID Server's software version is current
questions.explain: Re-certification is a full check of continued relevance, correct classification, and relationship accuracy — anything that fails gets flagged for decommission.

questions.q: Why does the upcoming course, ServiceNow Security & Access Controls, depend on this capstone's governance plan?
options: It doesn't — security policy is designed completely independently of CMDB data
Asset-based access policies, like who can touch SCHED-APP-01 or query SCHED-SQL-01, are only as reliable as the ownership and relationship data this capstone built and governs
Security Course 10 will rebuild its own separate CMDB from scratch
The next course only covers password policy, which has no connection to CI ownership
questions.explain: An access policy scoped to CI owners or specific CIs is exactly as trustworthy as the CMDB data behind it — which is what this governance plan is designed to keep accurate.
